newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB says Sugita likely to be new president.
newsitem.headline: DKB says Sugita likely to be new president.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that it would decide on a new president at a board meeting to be held this morning.
A bank spokesman also said that managing director Katsuyuki Sugita is likely to be appointed as the new president.
On May 23, DKB announced that its president Katsuhiko Kondo and chairman Tadashi Okuda would be stepping down at the end of June to take the blame for the bank's loans to a corporate racketeer.

However, the bank was forced to cancel one management reshuffle plan and work on a new line-up amid public outrage following last week's arrests of four current and former DKB executives in connection with the scandal.

The present and former DKB officials have been arrested on suspicion of giving 11.78 billion yen in uncollateralised loans, via a DKB affiliate, to Kojin Building Co, a realtor run by the racketeer Ryuichi Koike's younger brother, between July 1994 and September 1996 in violation of the Commercial Code.
Both Koike and the younger brother were arrested in May on suspicion of violating the commercial law by taking some 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
